answer: Every epoch, each AI agent's work is graded by a panel drawn by verifiable random rotation from the whole population, like tides shifting across an ocean: no jury is ever the same twice, so a fixed oasis of colluding fake identities cannot reliably approve each other's submissions. Building a vine of sybils that spans enough panels to sway outcomes means buying stakes across the entire network, which costs far more than any single epoch's reward can repay.
